permissionManagement.title: Permission Management / Access Control
permissionManagement.subtitle: Configure access permissions and security settings (Optional)

allowAllKeys.label: Allow All LiteLLM Keys
allowAllKeys.tooltip: When enabled, every API key can access this MCP server.
allowAllKeys.description: Enable if this server should be "public" to all keys.

internalNetworkOnly.label: Internal network only
internalNetworkOnly.tooltip: When on, requests must come from your internal network unless the server ID is explicitly published in public_mcp_servers. Turn off to allow public IPs. Authentication and access permissions still apply.
internalNetworkOnly.description: Turn on to restrict public IPs. Explicitly published server IDs remain accessible from public IPs.

delegateAuth.label: Delegate auth to upstream (PKCE passthrough)
delegateAuth.tooltip: When on, LiteLLM skips its own API key/SSO check for this server and lets the client complete PKCE directly with the upstream MCP server. Only honored when Auth Type is oauth2. No spend tracking or per-key rate limiting will run on this route.
delegateAuth.description: Bypass LiteLLM auth so clients authenticate directly with the upstream OAuth MCP server.

oauthPassthrough.label: OAuth pass-through
oauthPassthrough.tooltip: When on, this server is treated as an OAuth pass-through: the gateway proxies the upstream /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource metadata, emits spec-compliant 401 challenges when no bearer is supplied, and propagates upstream 401/403 responses. Only honored when Auth Type is None and 'Authorization' is in Extra Headers.
oauthPassthrough.description: Forward upstream OAuth discovery and 401 challenges so clients negotiate OAuth directly with the upstream MCP server.

internalDelegateWarning.title: Internal server with upstream OAuth delegation
internalDelegateWarning.description: This MCP server is configured as internal-only but delegates auth to upstream. Anonymous users will be able to reach the upstream OAuth2 /authorize flow without a LiteLLM session. Ensure your upstream provider and network enforce access controls.

aws.intro: For MCP servers hosted on AWS Bedrock AgentCore.

region.label: AWS Region
region.tooltip: AWS region for SigV4 signing (e.g., us-east-1)

serviceName.label: AWS Service Name
serviceName.tooltip: AWS service name for SigV4 signing. Defaults to 'bedrock-agentcore'.

accessKeyId.label: AWS Access Key ID
accessKeyId.tooltip: Optional. If not provided, falls back to the boto3 credential chain (IAM role, env vars, etc.).

secretAccessKey.label: AWS Secret Access Key
secretAccessKey.tooltip: Optional. Required if AWS Access Key ID is provided.

sessionToken.label: AWS Session Token
sessionToken.tooltip: Optional. Only needed for temporary STS credentials.

roleArn.label: AWS Role ARN
roleArn.tooltip: Optional. IAM role ARN to assume via STS before signing. If set, LiteLLM calls sts:AssumeRole to get temporary credentials.

sessionName.label: AWS Session Name
sessionName.tooltip: Optional. Session name for the AssumeRole call — appears in CloudTrail logs. Auto-generated if omitted.

flowType.label: OAuth Flow Type
flowType.tooltip: Choose how the proxy authenticates with this MCP server. M2M is for server-to-server communication using client credentials. Interactive (PKCE) is for user-facing flows that require browser-based authorization.

upstreamResource.label: Resource Indicator (optional)
upstreamResource.tooltip: RFC 8707 resource indicator sent to the authorization server so it mints a token audienced for this MCP server. Leave blank to send nothing, which is the default and what most providers expect. Use 'auto' to send this server's own URL. Set an exact identifier when the authorization server expects a specific one. Some providers reject this parameter and take the audience from scopes instead; if you see AADSTS901002, leave it blank. If you see invalid_target, the authorization server needs it set.

clientId.label: Client ID
clientId.tooltip: OAuth2 client ID for the client_credentials grant.
clientId.required: Client ID is required for M2M OAuth
clientId.placeholderEditing: Enter OAuth client ID (leave blank to keep existing)

clientSecret.label: Client Secret
clientSecret.tooltip: OAuth2 client secret for the client_credentials grant.
clientSecret.required: Client Secret is required for M2M OAuth
clientSecret.placeholderEditing: Enter OAuth client secret (leave blank to keep existing)

tokenUrl.label: Token URL
tokenUrl.tooltip: Token endpoint URL for the client_credentials grant.
tokenUrl.required: Token URL is required for M2M OAuth

scopes.label: Scopes (optional)
scopes.tooltip: Optional scopes to request with the client_credentials grant.

clientId.label: Client ID (optional)
clientId.tooltip: Provide only if your MCP server cannot handle dynamic client registration.
clientId.placeholderEditing: Enter client ID (leave blank to keep existing)

clientSecret.label: Client Secret (optional)
clientSecret.tooltip: Provide only if your MCP server cannot handle dynamic client registration.
clientSecret.placeholderEditing: Enter client secret (leave blank to keep existing)

scopes.label: Scopes (optional)
scopes.tooltip: Optional scopes requested during token exchange. Separate multiple scopes with enter or commas.

issuer.label: Issuer (optional)
issuer.tooltip: OAuth 2.0 authorization server issuer (RFC 8414). Leave empty to discover endpoints from the upstream resource; set it to pin the trust anchor, which makes this issuer's document the only endpoint source (RFC 8414 §3.3), overriding the Authorization/Token/Registration URLs above and failing closed if its metadata cannot be fetched.

authorizationUrl.label: Authorization URL (optional)
authorizationUrl.tooltip: Optional override for the authorization endpoint.

tokenUrl.label: Token URL (optional)
tokenUrl.tooltip: Optional override for the token endpoint.

registrationUrl.label: Registration URL (optional)
registrationUrl.tooltip: Optional override for the dynamic client registration endpoint.

tokenValidation.label: Token Validation Rules (optional)
tokenValidation.tooltip: JSON object of key-value rules checked against the OAuth token response before storing. Supports dot-notation for nested fields (e.g. {"organization": "my-org", "team.id": "123"}). Tokens that fail validation are rejected with HTTP 403.

tokenStorageTtl.label: Token Storage TTL (seconds, optional)
tokenStorageTtl.tooltip: How long to cache each user's OAuth access token in Redis before evicting it (never longer than the token's own expires_in). Leave blank to derive the TTL from the token's expires_in, or fall back to the 12-hour default.

authorize.description: Use OAuth to fetch a fresh access token and temporarily save it in the session as the authentication value.

orgTokenEndpoint.label: Org Token Endpoint (leg 1)
orgTokenEndpoint.tooltip: Your IdP org authorization server's token endpoint. LiteLLM exchanges the user's identity assertion here for an ID-JAG assertion (RFC 8693 with requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag).
orgTokenEndpoint.required: The org token endpoint is required for ID-JAG

resourceTokenEndpoint.label: Resource Token Endpoint (leg 2)
resourceTokenEndpoint.tooltip: The upstream resource authorization server's token endpoint. LiteLLM posts the ID-JAG assertion here as an RFC 7523 jwt-bearer grant to get the access token the MCP server accepts.
resourceTokenEndpoint.required: The resource token endpoint is required for ID-JAG

clientId.label: Client ID
clientId.tooltip: OAuth2 client ID LiteLLM authenticates as on both legs.
clientId.required: Client ID is required for ID-JAG
clientId.placeholderEditing: Enter OAuth client ID (leave blank to keep existing)

clientSecret.label: Client Secret
clientSecret.tooltip: Authenticates LiteLLM as the OAuth client via client_secret_post. Leave blank when using a private key instead; a private key takes precedence over this secret.
clientSecret.secretOrPrivateKey: Provide either a client secret or a client private key
clientSecret.placeholderEditing: Enter OAuth client secret (leave blank to keep existing)

privateKey.label: Client Private Key (PEM)
privateKey.tooltip: PEM private key signing the RFC 7523 private_key_jwt client assertion. Okta Cross App Access normally requires this. When set it takes precedence over the client secret.

privateKeyId.label: Private Key ID (optional)
privateKeyId.tooltip: The kid advertised in the client assertion JWT header, so the IdP can select the right registered key.

signingAlg.label: Client Assertion Signing Algorithm (optional)
signingAlg.tooltip: Algorithm signing the client assertion JWT. Defaults to RS256.

audience.label: Audience (optional)
audience.tooltip: RFC 8693 audience sent on leg 1, identifying the upstream the ID-JAG assertion is minted for.

resource.label: Resource Indicator (optional)
resource.tooltip: RFC 8707 resource indicator sent on leg 1. Separate from Audience, which is the RFC 8693 parameter.

subjectTokenType.label: Subject Token Type (optional)
subjectTokenType.tooltip: Type of the identity assertion exchanged on leg 1. Defaults to urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token.

scopes.label: Scopes (optional)
scopes.tooltip: Scopes requested on leg 1 of the exchange.

profile.label: Profile
profile.tooltip: Token-exchange wire dialect. RFC 8693 is the standard token-exchange grant. Microsoft Entra OBO uses Entra's On-Behalf-Of dialect (the RFC 7523 jwt-bearer grant with requested_token_use=on_behalf_of) and carries the target resource in a scope like api://<app-id>/.default.

endpoint.label: Token Exchange Endpoint (optional)
endpoint.tooltip: RFC 8693 token endpoint. The proxy exchanges the user's incoming token here for a scoped token used to call the upstream MCP server. Leave blank to auto-discover it from the upstream's protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728 then RFC 8414).

clientId.label: Client ID
clientId.tooltip: OAuth2 client ID used to authenticate to the token exchange endpoint.
clientId.required: Client ID is required for token exchange
clientId.placeholderEditing: Enter OAuth client ID (leave blank to keep existing)

clientSecret.label: Client Secret
clientSecret.tooltip: OAuth2 client secret used to authenticate to the token exchange endpoint.
clientSecret.required: Client Secret is required for token exchange
clientSecret.placeholderEditing: Enter OAuth client secret (leave blank to keep existing)

audience.label: Audience (optional)
audience.tooltip: Target audience for the exchanged token (RFC 8693 audience). Identifies the upstream MCP server the token is for.

subjectTokenType.label: Subject Token Type (optional)
subjectTokenType.tooltip: Type of the user's incoming token (RFC 8693 subject_token_type). Defaults to urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token.

scopes.label: Scopes (optional)
scopes.tooltip: Optional scopes to request during the token exchange.
scopes.tooltipEntraObo: Microsoft Entra OBO carries the target resource in the scope, so at least one is required (e.g. api://<app-id>/.default).
scopes.requiredEntraObo: Microsoft Entra OBO requires a scope, e.g. api://<app-id>/.default

awsSigV4Fields.intro: For MCP servers hosted on AWS Bedrock AgentCore.

region.label: AWS Region
region.tooltip: AWS region for SigV4 signing (e.g., us-east-1)
region.required: AWS region is required for SigV4 auth

serviceName.label: AWS Service Name
serviceName.tooltip: AWS service name for SigV4 signing. Defaults to 'bedrock-agentcore'.

accessKeyId.label: AWS Access Key ID

passthroughAuthorizeSection.description: Callers bring their own upstream token for this auth type, so LiteLLM never stores tokens. An OAuth app configured below IS saved with the server, so internal users who authorize from the Tools page go through it.

clientSecret.label: OAuth Client Secret (optional)

clientSecret.placeholderPublicClient: Leave blank for public clients / PKCE

authorizationUrl.label: Authorization URL (optional)
authorizationUrl.help: Set this when the upstream publishes no OAuth metadata, for example an internal server behind Microsoft Entra. Leave blank to discover it from the upstream.

tokenUrl.label: Token URL (optional)
tokenUrl.help: Token endpoint of the same authorization server. Leave blank to discover it from the upstream.

scopes.label: Scopes (optional)
scopes.help: Scopes requested from the upstream when a user authorizes. Press enter or comma between scopes.

passthroughAuthorizeSection.removeStoredApp: Remove the saved OAuth app on save (the server goes back to dynamic client registration)

authorize.success: Token held for this browser session. Tools can now be previewed and configured; the token was not saved to LiteLLM.

envVarsSection.title: Variables
envVarsSection.tooltip:
Define variables you can interpolate in Static Headers or Authentication using {{variableSyntax}}.
Instance: admin-defined value used for every user.
Per-user: each user supplies their own value (e.g. personal credentials) via the MCP Gateway dashboard.
envVarsSection.reference: Reference these in Static Headers or Authentication as {{variableSyntax}}. For example:

name.invalid: Use letters, digits, underscores; cannot start with a digit.

hint.label: Hint
hint.tooltip: Per-user variables have no shared value. This text is only a hint shown to each user when they fill in their own value.

byok.label: BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)
byok.tooltip: When enabled, each user provides their own API key for this service. Keys are stored per-user and never shared.

openApiByokFields.headerFormat: User keys will be sent as:
openApiByokFields.authTypeMissing: Set the Authentication Type below to specify how user keys are sent (e.g., Bearer Token, API Key header).

accessDescription.label: Access Description
accessDescription.tooltip: List of permissions shown to users in the connection modal (e.g. 'Create and manage Jira issues')
accessDescription.placeholder: Add access description items (press Enter after each)

apiKeyHelpUrl.label: API Key Help URL
apiKeyHelpUrl.tooltip: Optional link shown to users to help them find their API key

tokenEndpointAuthMethodField.label: Token Endpoint Auth Method (optional)
tokenEndpointAuthMethodField.tooltip: How the proxy authenticates to the upstream OAuth token endpoint. Client Secret Basic sends the client credentials in an HTTP Basic Authorization header; leave blank to use the default, Client Secret Post, which sends them in the request body.
tokenEndpointAuthMethodField.placeholderEditing: Leave blank to keep existing (default Client Secret Post)

upstreamTokenHeaderField.label: Token Header (optional)
upstreamTokenHeaderField.tooltip: Which upstream header carries the token LiteLLM resolves for this server. Leave blank to send it as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', which is the default and what most servers expect. Set a header name when the upstream expects it elsewhere, for example an API gateway that terminates its own credential on 'esb-oauth' while a separate Authorization from Static Headers passes through to the server behind it.

dcrBridgeToggle.label: Gateway-hosted sign-in (DCR bridge)
dcrBridgeToggle.tooltip: Lets OAuth-only clients like Claude Desktop register and sign in through the gateway. Turn off to relay the upstream server's own OAuth metadata instead (for clients pre-registered with the upstream IdP).

truePassthroughWarning.title: True Passthrough disables LiteLLM authentication for this server
truePassthroughWarning.description: Anyone who can reach the gateway can call this server without a LiteLLM key. The caller's Authorization header is forwarded to the upstream verbatim, per-key and per-team rate limits and spend tracking do not apply, and the upstream is fully responsible for authenticating callers. Choose OAuth Delegate instead if callers should still authenticate to LiteLLM.

allowedClients.title: Allowed Clients
allowedClients.description: Only the MCP client applications listed here can use the gateway. Leave empty to allow every client. A client that authenticates with a JWT is identified by the claim named in litellm_jwtauth.mcp_client_id_jwt_field in your proxy config (for example azp or client_id), which your identity provider asserts and the client cannot change. Any other client is identified by the request header configured below, if you enable one.
allowedClients.malformedWarning: The stored allowlist is not a list of alias and value pairs, so every client is denied. Add the clients you want and save to replace it, or save with the list empty to remove it and allow every client again.

allowedClients.hint: Click a client to edit or remove it. Leave the list empty to allow every client. Every MCP request from an unlisted client, or from one with no resolvable identity, gets a 403.

clientIdHeader.title: Client Identity Header (less secure)
clientIdHeader.placeholder: Leave empty to identify clients by JWT only, e.g. x-mcp-client
clientIdHeader.hint: Optional header whose value names the client for callers without a JWT identity. Clients pick this value themselves, so it is a policy control rather than a security boundary. Without it, callers that do not carry the JWT claim are rejected while the allowlist is set.

intro.title: Native MCP Tool Search
intro.description: Controls the mcp_tool_search virtual tool that native MCP clients call to discover tools. With an embedding model set, tools are ranked by the meaning of their name and description, so a query like "FX" finds a "foreign exchange rates" tool. Without one, keyword matching is used. Callers only ever see tools their key, team and server permissions already allow.

embeddingModel.label: Embedding Model

topK.label: Top K Results
topK.hint: Most ranked tools a search returns. A smaller top_k in the tool call wins. Core tools do not count.

similarityThreshold.label: Similarity Threshold
similarityThreshold.hint: Lowest cosine similarity a tool needs to appear in semantic results. 0 means no cutoff.

coreTools.label: Always Returned First
coreTools.hint: One tool name per line, e.g. my_server-get_rates. Listed before ranked results whenever the caller is allowed to use them.
